## TL;DR
The release update dialog now shows the correct upgrade command with a Copy button, backed by `installKind` and `upgradeCommand` on `GET /api/release/available`, computed by one exported helper shared with `repoos upgrade`. The last fix removes a version assertion from a route test that broke when the repo version moved on.

## Work and rationale
`upgradeInstruction` in `src/commands/upgrade.ts` detects standalone, package-manager, source and channel installs, and the route feeds it the same root and version `repoos upgrade` uses. The dialog shows the command with a Copy button (keyboard accessible, empty command is a failed copy), the old button is relabelled "Release notes", and the dismissed version persists in localStorage. At close-out the standalone-install route test failed because it asserted `currentVersion: "0.5.79"`, but the offline payload reports the build's own version, which changed after v0.5.80. The assertion tested nothing about install detection, so it was removed; `installKind` and `upgradeCommand` are still asserted.

## Approaches tried
Detection by version alone cannot tell a built checkout from a curl install, so a structural probe (`.git` or `src` plus `package.json` beside the install root) is used. Package-manager paths are matched first.

## Challenges and blockers
Five review passes, mostly repeating edge cases of the same class, and a handoff collision with the engineer's own check. The close-out test failure only reproduced against the branch merged with main, because the version hard-coded in the test no longer matched.

## Key learnings
Tests of install detection must not assert the repo's own version. Reproduce close-out failures on the branch merged with main, not the branch alone.
